summary: Two shell traps in one script, and only one was a syntax error. Writing branch-health.sh hit IFS=$'\t', which is a bashism: dash reads it as the four literal characters $ ' \ t and splits fields on ANY of them, so 'Deploy Application' was reported as a workflow called 'Deploy Applica' and one row printed instead of four — while exiting 0. sh -n cannot see it. The second was an unbalanced quote that parsed fine until RUNTIME, ~100 lines after all the useful output, turning a correct exit 1 into a confusing exit 2. AGENTS.md invokes these scripts as `sh` and /bin/sh is dash here, so a #!/usr/bin/env bash shebang is a promise the invocation never keeps. Guarded by shell-portability.test.ts, which does both a parse check and a pattern scan and DERIVES its scope (shebang says sh, or something invokes it as sh) — the first draft checked every script and failed 12 honest bash ones, and flagged [[:space:]] as a bash [[ test
